# WAS_mme_MLP { #wass2s.WAS_mme_MLP }

```python
WAS_mme_MLP(
    search_method='random',
    hidden_layer_sizes_range=[(2,), (4,), (2, 4), (8,), (8, 16), (16,)],
    activation_options=['relu', 'tanh', 'identity'],
    learning_rate_init_range=loguniform(0.0001, 0.01),
    solver_options=['adam', 'sgd', 'lbfgs'],
    alpha_range=[0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1],
    max_iter=200,
    random_state=42,
    dist_method='nonparam',
    n_iter_search=10,
    cv_folds=3,
    n_clusters=4,
    early_stopping_options=[True, False],
    validation_fraction=0.1,
    n_iter_no_change=10,
    leave_one_year_out=False,
    optuna_n_jobs=None,
    optuna_timeout=None,
    n_jobs=-1,
    cv_n_jobs=-1,
)
```

Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLPRegressor) MME forecaster with per-zone
hyperparameter tuning and tercile-probability dressing. Deterministic
hindcast via compute_model; tercile probabilities via compute_prob
('nonparam' or 'bestfit'). Mirrors the WAS_mme_RF / WAS_mme_XGBoosting
contract so it plugs into the same_kind_model2 branch of WAS_Cross_Validator.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name          | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                               | Default   |
|---------------|--------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| n_jobs        | int    | Maximum number of parallel workers for grid/random search. ``-1`` uses all available CPUs (default is 4). MLPRegressor itself has no ``n_jobs`` parameter, so this controls parallel hyperparameter fits. | `-1`      |
| optuna_n_jobs | int    | Optional Optuna-specific worker count. When ``None``, it inherits ``n_jobs`` (default is None).                                                                                                           | `None`    |

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [calculate_tercile_probabilities_bestfit](#wass2s.WAS_mme_MLP.calculate_tercile_probabilities_bestfit) | Tercile probabilities from a forecast-adjusted best-fit family. |
| [calculate_tercile_probabilities_nonparametric](#wass2s.WAS_mme_MLP.calculate_tercile_probabilities_nonparametric) | Non-parametric tercile probabilities from historical error samples. |
| [compute_hyperparameters](#wass2s.WAS_mme_MLP.compute_hyperparameters) | Per-zone hyperparameter tuning. KMeans on predictand VALUES (kept). |
| [compute_model](#wass2s.WAS_mme_MLP.compute_model) | Deterministic hindcast per zone. Inputs are assumed standardized (the |
| [compute_prob](#wass2s.WAS_mme_MLP.compute_prob) | Tercile probabilities for a (cross-validated) deterministic hindcast. |
| [forecast](#wass2s.WAS_mme_MLP.forecast) | Deterministic + probabilistic forecast for a single target year. |
| [weibull_shape_solver](#wass2s.WAS_mme_MLP.weibull_shape_solver) | Root function for the Weibull shape k matching observed V/M^2. |

```python
WAS_mme_MLP.calculate_tercile_probabilities_bestfit(
    best_guess,
    error_variance,
    T1,
    T2,
    dist_code,
    dof,
)
```

Tercile probabilities from a forecast-adjusted best-fit family.

### compute_hyperparameters { #wass2s.WAS_mme_MLP.compute_hyperparameters }

```python
WAS_mme_MLP.compute_hyperparameters(
    Predictors,
    Predictand,
    clim_year_start=None,
    clim_year_end=None,
)
```

Per-zone hyperparameter tuning. KMeans on predictand VALUES (kept).

A dual-mode: clim years given -> standardize Predictors / Predictand
internally; both None -> assume already standardized (framework path),
so no double-standardization when called from compute_model.

### compute_model { #wass2s.WAS_mme_MLP.compute_model }

```python
WAS_mme_MLP.compute_model(
    X_train,
    y_train,
    X_test,
    y_test=None,
    clim_year_start=None,
    clim_year_end=None,
    best_params=None,
    cluster_da=None,
)
```

Deterministic hindcast per zone. Inputs are assumed standardized (the
same_kind_model2 branch standardizes once). A: clim_year_start/end
are in the signature, so the best_params=None path no longer raises.
